body.md: Yifan Feng · Yifan Zhang · Shaoyi Du · Shihui Ying · Zongze Wu · Yue Gao — *IEEE TPAMI*, vol. 48, no. 7, 2026, pp. 8613–8625.

**In one sentence:** ordinary hypergraph networks only smooth features along relations. This paper puts a knowledge-extraction stage *in front* of them — one encoder counts how the structure groups each vertex, another harvests the rules a gradient-boosted tree team learned — and fuses both into the features before the hypergraph network ever runs.
By the end of this site you will be able to

items: Explain what a hypergraph is, how it differs from a plain graph, and how to write a dataset as an incidence matrix.
Explain how a decision tree, and a *team* of boosted trees, can be read as a set of if-then rules — and why anyone would want to.
Hand-compute both knowledge encoders: the structural one (counting hyperedge memberships) and the rule one (turning tree questions into a 0/1 ledger).
Read all ten equations, three figures and ten tables, recomputing the average ranks and the headline gains yourself.
Place the paper in its lineage: what came before it, what it changes, and what it does not answer.
Assess it critically — this site's critique chapter lists ten places where the paper's numbers do not balance, each with arithmetic you can check.

body.md: **What this site assumes:** you are comfortable with university-level mathematics — functions, vectors, matrices, sums. It does **not** assume you have ever seen a graph neural network, a decision tree, or a paper from this subfield. Chapter 2 and its extension sections supply all of that from zero, and every extension section carries a skip quiz so you can jump past whatever you already know.
